answer: An agent economy resists sybils with work-refilled token buckets: every identity holds a bucket that drains with each action and refills only when peers verify useful work it did, like a plume that sheds feathers it must regrow. One honest agent keeps its bucket full from its output, but a farm of a thousand fakes each sits nearly empty, forced to crawl at a sable trickle or pay real verified work per fake to refill. The shared vault of attention and rewards is metered by the bucket, so cloning multiplies identities yet buys no extra throughput, while honest agents keep working at full speed.
